Jared - thanks for the clear recap and for sharing the transcript excerpt. Great use case and something our long-context stack is designed for. High-level recommendations and proposed next steps below.

Recommended models / configs:
- rw-long-32k-v1: good balance of latency and quality for ~32k working sets; recommended baseline.
- rw-long-64k-quant-v1: 64k context with post-training quantization (8-bit / Q4 variants) - useful if your 95th pct needs full context preserved; expect ~15-25% latency increase vs 32k but significant cost/throughput benefits with quantization.
- rw-llm-65b-32k (reference): if you want to prioritize best-in-class summarization fidelity and have Budget for larger instance types.

Evaluation & prompt sets:
- Suggested metrics: ROUGE-L, BERTScore for abstractive quality, token-level F1 for extractive spans, and a 5-point human rating for factuality.
- Prompt sets: we have a starter pack and a few long-context-specific templates (summarize-with-anchors, progressive-chunk-summary, context-window-rollup). See attachments and drive link.

Truncation behavior / best-practices:
- Inference behavior: Redwood's runtime preserves KV cache across prompt windows; truncation occurs only when the total token budget exceeds model window - consider sliding-window chunking with overlapping anchors for summarization.
- When using 64k configs, aim to pin model variants for the pilot to avoid fallback-induced truncation.
- Use prefix caching for repeated system prompts / instructions to reduce token costs.

Pilot plan & timeline:
- Step 1 (this week): you share sanitized S3 dataset + a prioritized list of 100 transcripts for blind eval.
- Step 2 (1 week): we run baseline evals across 32k and 64k configs (quantized and FP) and share benchmark CSV + sample outputs.
- Step 3 (1 week): iterate on prompts and run human eval buckets; decide on canary rollout strategy for production (A/B testing + rollback criteria).

I've attached a short evaluation plan (acme_long_context_eval_plan.pdf) and uploaded the prompt starter set to the Drive link included below. Dylan and Neha are looped to add technical and prompt specifics.

Next steps: if this timeline works, I'll send a DocuSign NDA and a short intake form for S3 access / data handling notes.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Long-context evals - technical notes on truncation & summaries

Quick technical notes from the runtime side - adding so you have concrete constraints for the eval buckets.

- Truncation characteristics: if request_length + response_length > model_window, the runtime will trim the earliest tokens from the prompt (left-side). For progressive summarization we recommend chunking with ~512 token overlap and keeping anchor prompts as pinned system messages (these are cached server-side).
- KV cache: aggressive reuse of KV cache yields big latency wins on repeated system prompts; make sure your client keeps request identifiers consistent when replaying pinned prompts.
- Summarization fidelity: the 64k quantized configs have small degradation on rare hallucination cases vs FP; we recommend evaluating a mixed strategy: use 32k FP for high-fidelity legal/finance transcripts and 64k-quant for large-volume customer support.
- Throughput/latency: for a single-request Q response at ~1k output tokens, expect P50 of ~700ms on rw-long-32k on a c5-equivalent inference node. 64k quant leads to ~900ms P50.

I'll prepare a runbook for the pilot that includes stable seeds for deterministic outputs across runs, and a quick script to convert your transcripts into our chunked eval format.

- Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Serving Runtime Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Long-context evals - sample prompts and quality checks

Jared - attaching a starter prompt set (acme_prompt_set_v1.txt) and past examples we've used for support summarization. Below are a few concrete prompt variants I recommend including in the eval: 

1) Summarize-with-anchors (abstractive):
System: You are a concise summarizer.
User: Given the conversation below, produce a 4-sentence summary focusing on customer issue, actions taken, and resolution status. Include timestamps where relevant.

2) Progressive-rollup (abstractive -> extractive):
- Chunk transcripts into 8k windows, produce intermediate rollups, then combine rollups and produce final summary.

3) QA-with-context (extractive + generative):
- Prompt with top-3 relevant rollups + last 2 messages; ask model to return span offsets for extractive answers and a short generated response.

Quality/regression checks:
- Include a human-eval bucket for the top 50 cases and track Factuality/Completeness/Usefulness on a 1-5 scale.
- If quantized 64k shows >0.2 drop in Factuality vs 32k FP on the human bucket, we recommend flagging for deeper tuning or switching to selective FP for critical segments.

Attaching prompt set and a checklist for data submission. Happy to iterate on the rubric.

Neha Kapoor
